provider: DSpace 7+ platform class (MIT, UCT, demo.dspace.org and ~3,485 registered sites)

free_tier.stated: NO QUOTA CONCEPT AT ALL. The string 'quota' does not appear once in DSpace's 2,125-line dspace.cfg; the only two hits repo-wide are a Solr query-parser class and a discovery.cfg comment. There is no per-user, per-collection or per-installation storage limit in the software. The only byte constraint is a per-request multipart limit.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

chaining: Unbounded by construction. But every instance's write path is affiliation-gated in practice, and the registry is dominated by pre-7 installs with no REST API at all.
limits_note: per-object-cap 512 MB/file in DSpace 7+ (spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size = 512MB, max-request-size = 512MB). DSpace 6 and below used upload.max, which accepts -1 for 'no limit'.
reliability_note: 60 of 60 sampled registry sites returned no /server/api/info, i.e. they are DSpace 6 or earlier and expose no modern REST API. The registry is a lagging indicator of what is programmatically usable.

extras.agent_focus: Systematic sweep of self-hosted academic repository software (Dataverse, DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, Fedora/Islandora) scored on the four client questions: institutional-email requirement, per-file cap, per-collection/dataset cap, and whether the install enforces a quota object at all. Primary method was machine probing, not page reading: /api/info/version and /api/dataverses/:root/storage/quota?showInherited=true against the full official Dataverse installation registry (150 hostnames), the native-signup form probe /dataverseuser.xhtml?editMode=CREATE against all 83 no-quota hosts, and the platform source defaults read out of the upstream config files for DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, libp2p and iroh. Secondary coverage of the relay/P2P half of the slot.

binding_note: the quota is real and unreachable: identity is the binding constraint, and it is not one of the six limits kinds
